Jules (Eng): Hey @people-ops — returning from 12 weeks of paid parental leave next Monday. We finalized an adoption while I was out. Can I add the child to benefits now or do I have to wait until open enrollment?
Riley (People Ops): Congrats on the adoption! Short answer: adoption finalization is a QLE. You have 30 days from the adoption finalization date to enroll the child outside open enrollment. Do you have the adoption finalization paperwork?
Jules (Eng): Yes  court decree dated 2026-02-15. We finalized while I was on leave. I thought the leave paperwork would auto-add them.
Marta (Benefits): Nice news 44f. Adoption is covered as a QLE for medical, dental, vision, and dependent care FSA. You should submit a QLE via the benefits portal and attach the court decree. Coverage is effective as of the finalization date if you enroll within the 30-day window.
Jules (Eng): Okay. Two follow-ups: 1) I changed my FSA elections before leave; can I increase dependent care FSA midyear because daycare starts now? 2) My payroll people are on vacation this week  will retro premium adjustments wait?
Marta (Benefits): 1) Yes, dependent care FSA can be changed midyear with a QLE that affects dependent care (like adoption). You can increase or open a dependent care election; it will be prorated from the effective date. 2) Payroll timing: we send the retro-adjust request to payroll after Benefits approves. If payroll processing is delayed because of staffing, adjustments will still be applied but might appear on the next available cycle.
Jules (Eng): Great. What about HSA? I'm on an HDHP and was contributing individually before leave. Now family coverage would change HSA limits. Do I need to update my HSA election too?
Marta (Benefits): Good catch. If you switch coverage tier (employee-only -> employee+child or family), you should update HSA contributions to stay within IRS limits. Employer HSA contributions are also prorated. If you exceed contribution limits because of midyear changes, we can advise on how to correct. Recommend updating payroll elections asap after enrollment.
Jules (Eng): The child's SSN is pending  adoption agency says it may take 4-6 weeks to get. Is SSN required to enroll?
Riley (People Ops): SSN is not required at initial submission. Upload the court decree and a birth certificate (or agency letter) and mark SSN pending. We can provisionally enroll the child and update SSN later. If there's a long delay, include the SSN application receipt and we can grant an exception window.
Jules (Eng): Do I need to upload anything else (proof of residence, etc.)?
Marta (Benefits): For adoptive children we usually need the decree and birth certificate/agency placement letter. Proof of residence only if the dependent is claimed under special custody rules. Please include a short note: "Adoption QLE - provisional SSN pending."
Jules (Eng): Where exactly do I upload? Filename tips?
Riley (People Ops): Benefits portal -> Manage Dependents -> Add Dependent (QLE). File names that help triage: jules-green-adoption-decree.pdf, jules-green-birthcert.pdf. If you must send large scans, use the portal SFTP link and paste the SFTP receipt in the submission notes.
Jules (Eng): If I miss the 30-day window because I was on leave and didn't see the email, can you backdate?
Riley (People Ops): We do accept late QLEs in cases where the employee was out on company-approved leave and missed the window, but you must provide proof of the leave dates (HR leave record) and adoption finalization date. People Ops + Benefits review exceptions case-by-case; payroll retro-adjustment may still apply if approved.
Jules (Eng): Will adding the child affect my taxes for the year? Any interaction with claiming as a dependent vs benefits enrollment?
Marta (Benefits): Benefits enrollment is separate from IRS dependent claims. However, dependent care FSA and pre-tax benefits have tax implications. For example, dependent care FSA is limited and must match eligible expenses. We recommend consulting a tax advisor if you're claiming the child as a tax dependent. We can provide plan-specific forms if needed.
Jules (Eng): Thanks. Last: daycare will start 2026-03-15. If I open dependent care FSA now, can I submit claims dating back to the adoption date or only from daycare start?
Marta (Benefits): Dependent care FSA reimbursements are for eligible expenses incurred after the election effective date. If you open the DC FSA with an effective date equal to the adoption finalization date, you could be reimbursed for eligible expenses incurred from that date forward. You cannot claim expenses prior to the effective date.

Riley (People Ops): Congrats again! We'll review within 3 business days and ping back in-thread. If you need expedited processing, DM me and include the SFTP receipt. :)
